description: This 2025 study shows that accurate GNSS positioning, under 1 to 2 m horizontal error, is feasible beneath closed-canopy conifer forests 40 to 60 m tall in western Washington state when survey-grade receivers are occupied for at least 15 minutes, whereas short occupations with budget receivers are generally inaccurate, with horizontal errors above 5 to 20 m. It also demonstrates the effects of receiver height, occupation duration, base-station distance and differential post-processing mode (autonomous, code, fixed-integer and floating-point) on horizontal accuracy, using a geodetic survey as the accuracy benchmark. Producer: US Forest Service Pacific Northwest Research Station, published in Remote Sensing Applications: Society and Environment volume 37 (article 101428). Coverage: western Washington conifer forests. Access: PDF (14 MB) free on the USFS Treesearch page. Licence and cost: free; no licence statement was read. Caveats: the geodetic benchmark is hard for other users to replicate, and the underlying observation data were not confirmed as downloadable. Simulation uses: the accuracy results by receiver setting support validation of canopy multipath and positioning-error models. Related records: none linked.
